title: 08 Modes Folk

blocks.text: Modes explain tunes that don't behave like textbook major or minor — central to authentic Irish and Scottish harmonisation.
Minor 3rd, major 6th. A dorian: A B C D E F♯ G A. 'Banish Misfortune' often analysed as A dorian.
Major 3rd, flat 7th. D mixolydian: D E F♯ G A B C D. Many D-centred tunes use C natural.
Don't sharp the characteristic flat note. Mode-aware backup keeps sessions sounding authentic.

sections.title: Q1. D dorian vs D natural minor:

blocks.text:
- A) Major sixth
- B) Lowered third
- C) No fourth
- D) Extra sharps

**Answer:** A

sections.title: Q2. Mixolydian lowers the 7th vs major.

### Q1. D dorian vs D natural minor:

- A) Major sixth
- B) Lowered third
- C) No fourth
- D) Extra sharps

**Answer:** A

### Q2. Mixolydian lowers the 7th vs major.

**Answer:** True
